text.text_excerpt: I grew up visiting the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas many times as a kid. Now that we are older we can bring my nephews here and they can be at awe of the fishes. The Aquarium is a great clean facility and fun for the whole family. It is very expensive though and to get the most out of your experience I definitely recommend you take your time and also watch one of the IMAX movies. The one based on Hurricane Katrina is quite interesting and the swamp scenes are cool. The Aquarium is divided into a few sections. Honestly, I feel like it is quite small for what you pay for. This was a really great aquarium. I had a really good time. The tanks were all clean and the staff was friendly. It only took about an hour to cruise through and see all the different aquariums. I loved the penguin exhibit. I just think they are so cute and I really enjoyed watching them interact. Lots of cool fish in all sizes, shapes, and colors. I especially enjoyed all the varieties of seahorses. They are really fun to watch. And the stingrays were great too. I like how the aquarium is laid out by sections of the world. They had a huge anaconda. Lots of eels also. Even the electric eel. And you have to have an alligator, or it just wouldn't be Louisiana. The huge tank downstairs is am...

I like the structure of this aquarium -- the way the exhibits flow from one to another. $20 per person for a couple hours inside (mostly visiting the white alligator and viewing the various shark tanks) was money well spent. In addition to the fishes, there were also a lot of birds both in their own exhibits and sprinkled throughout the others. I was particularly excited to spot an owl but, honestly, I could have spent hours with the sharks. I'm a fan. The penguins were on vacation while we were there because their exhibit is undergoing refurbishment.
